question.problem:
We wish to construct a cylindrical can with a base but no lid. Our cylinder must have an exact volume of $8\pi \,{in}^{3}.$ What is the smallest possible surface area ${S}_{\text{min}}$ of the cylinder? Do not round the answer.

${S}_{\text{min}}=$
{{field-1}} ${\text{in}}^{2}$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's draw a picture of a cylinder. Let $r$ be the radius, and $h$ the height.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14195873/assets/7fe5dad64f7c065e693ed407e0f291ec995b4823a0356e11055d20a0ca89a53b.png)

We wish to minimize the surface area

$$
S=2\pi rh+\pi {r}^{2}.
$$

We know that the volume is fixed at $8\pi \,{in}^{3},$ so we also have the constraint condition

$$
8\pi =\pi {r}^{2}h.
$$

Now, by making $h$ the subject of the constraint equation, we have that

$$
h=\frac{8}{{r}^{2}}.
$$

Plugging the above into our expression for $S,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}S(r) & =2\pi r(\frac{8}{{r}^{2}})+\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =\frac{16\pi }{r}+\pi {r}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We want to minimize $S,$ so we need to differentiate $S$ and set the derivative equal to zero. The derivative is 

$$
{S}^{′}(r)=-\frac{16\pi }{{r}^{2}}+2\pi r.
$$

Setting the derivative equal to zero and solving for $r$ gives a stationary point, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}^{′}(r) & =0 \\ -\frac{16\pi }{{r}^{2}}+2\pi r & =0 \\ 2\pi r & =\frac{16\pi }{{r}^{2}} \\ 2\pi {r}^{3} & =16\pi  \\ {r}^{3} & =8 \\ r & =\sqrt[3]{8} \\ r & =2\,\text{in}\end{aligned}
$$

Using a calculator, we can verify that if $r<2$ then ${S}^{′}(r)<0,$ and if $r>2$ then ${S}^{′}(r)>0,$ which means that the stationary point $r=2$ is indeed a minimum of $S(r).$

Finally, to find the smallest surface area ${S}_{\text{min}},$ we substitute $r=2\,\text{in}$ into the equation for the surface area $S:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{\text{min}}=S(2) & =\frac{16\pi }{2}+\pi (2)^{2} \\  & =8\pi +4\pi  \\  & =12\pi \,{\text{in}}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$
